PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Use the SDK 1.0.14 owned runtime
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- removes the explicit `@github/copilot` runtime dependency from root and remote manifests
- uses the runtime owned by `@github/copilot-sdk@1.0.14` (`copilotCliVersion: 1.0.85`)
- packages and launches `@github/copilot-sdk-<platform>/prebuilds/<platform>/copilot-runtime` with its adjacent `runtime.node`
- keeps both native files outside ASAR so Microsoft product signing signs both
- updates universal macOS cross-copy/merge handling and Linux package dependency snapshots
- couples SDK canary overrides to the runtime version declared by the SDK and rejects shell metacharacters in canary version inputs
- preserves the two supported runtime-owned built-in skills and project/plugin skills through explicit session skill directories
- explicitly forwards directory-backed plugin hooks through the SDK callback surface
- rejects stale model selections against an available provider catalog before dispatching a model request

This does not use the standalone Node SEA and does not extract runtime code into the user-global Copilot cache.

The SDK-owned runtime still does not invoke plugin hook callbacks on Windows. Those seven Windows variants remain precisely gated and documented in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`; Unix callback behavior is active and verified exactly once.

## Local validation

Passed:
- `npm run hygiene`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run typecheck --prefix build`
- targeted ESLint
- complete deterministic Agent Host E2E matrix: Conformance, Claude, Codex, and Copilot
- Copilot prompt snapshots and skill-budget behavior: 23/23
- SDK runtime packaging tests: 23/23
- complete CopilotAgent unit suite: 388 passing, 1 expected pending; targeted launcher/runtime tests: 12/12
- structural audit of all 19 prompt baselines: identical tool and supported built-in capability sets
- unsafe Windows canary version input is rejected before npm execution

## Remote validation

- GitHub Code OSS run 35311420025 passed on the reviewed head.
- ADO Product build 474933 passed on the reviewed head across Windows x64, Linux x64/ARM64, and macOS x64/ARM64/universal; publishing and release were disabled.
- Earlier build 474817 validated the SDK-only packaging/signing layout and signed both `copilot-runtime` and adjacent `runtime.node` on macOS.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call path and network boundary are explicit in repository code, and the scheduler establishes realistic periodic and activity-driven overlap. Exact service latency and how often users switch during that overlap are uncertain, so severity is low rather than suppressing the finding.
Findings.PerformanceResource: A Copilot runtime `models.list` RPC and its backing network request
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Every model-change request that overlaps the 30-minute activity-gated refresh, an authentication/token refresh, or a client-restart refresh inherits the full remaining latency of that shared network request; concurrent model changes all remain blocked behind the same request.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased model-switch latency and a blocked user action when catalog enumeration is slow or stalled
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, `_changeModelOnce` resolved the chat and queued the SDK `setModel` operation immediately; background catalog refreshes did not gate the model-selection action.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: `_validateModelSelection` now awaits any scheduled or in-flight catalog refresh before even entering the per-chat queue, despite an already populated `_models` snapshot being available for validation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 5104 directly inserts `await (this._scheduledModelRefresh?.deferred.p ?? this._modelRefreshInFlight);` on every `changeModel` call; no equivalent wait existed before the PR.
Findings.Title: Do not await background catalog refreshes before switching models
Findings.Impact: Selecting a model while a periodic, token-driven, or restart-driven refresh is in flight now waits for `client.rpc.models.list`; the scheduler explicitly documents this as a real network request. On a slow connection or service hiccup, the model picker action can pause for that request even though the current catalog already contains the selected model.
Findings.Evidence: The added await reads `_scheduledModelRefresh?.deferred.p ?? _modelRefreshInFlight`. Those promises run `_refreshModels`, which calls `_listModels`, which awaits `client.rpc.models.list({ gitHubToken })`. `AgentModelRefreshScheduler` starts this real network request after active turns and every 30 minutes. The existing Codex model-resolution path demonstrates the bounded pattern: it starts/waits for refresh only when its model collection is empty.
Findings.Recommendation: Validate synchronously against the already populated `_models` snapshot, and only await/start catalog loading when the snapshot is empty or has been explicitly invalidated. Keep refresh coalescing and stale-generation handling unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switching the model for an existing Copilot chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed path now awaits `_scheduledModelRefresh` or `_modelRefreshInFlight`, then enters the per-chat sequencer, performs the SDK set-model operation, and persists metadata. The catalog await is newly on the user-action critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate the provider catalog through `client.rpc.models.list({ gitHubToken })`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one globally coalesced catalog request is in flight, but every overlapping model-change caller waits for it; refreshes are activity-gated and can occur on first/stale turn, every 30 minutes of active use, token changes, and client restarts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Catalog refreshes ran in the background and model changes proceeded directly to the existing per-chat SDK/persistence path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The full remaining request latency blocks the model-selection action before its chat queue starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Set the selected model on the live runtime session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK operation per model change, serialized by chat key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One serialized SDK set-model operation per selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing required model-switch operation; unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one metadata write per applicable model change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing required persistence after the SDK operation; unchanged by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The cost scales with the number of selections overlapping a refresh and, for each, with remaining network latency rather than model count. Effective boundary cardinality remains one coalesced request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model catalog refresh is globally coalesced to one request; model changes wait together on it and then remain serialized per chat through `_queueChat`. There is no added request fan-out, but the shared request now gates all overlapping selections.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `_models` retains the last-known successful catalog, including across transient failures, but the added await does not use that warm snapshot to avoid waiting. Empty catalogs fail open after refresh handling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added await, scheduler triggers, coalescing, and real network RPC are directly traced in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Overlap frequency and service latency vary; the critical-path dependency is explicit, but typical delay is unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity latency regression: an already warm catalog no longer prevents an unrelated background network refresh from blocking model selection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold Copilot client startup and session create/resume
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Client acquisition resolves packaged runtime paths, obtains telemetry configuration, spawns one SDK-owned runtime subprocess, then creates or resumes sessions. Session config includes two built-in skill directories and plugin metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe runtime executable, native module, SDK wrapper, built-in skill root, and two SKILL.md files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six successful local access checks for the selected package; Linux may probe the alternate libc candidate first, but short-circuits after its first missing runtime file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One access check per candidate for the standalone CLI entry point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: One-time local filesystem probing before runtime spawn; bounded and small relative to subprocess startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn the Copilot runtime over stdio
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced runtime process per client lifecycle, with a bounded startup-config retry path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Spawned one standalone Copilot CLI runtime process over stdio.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required startup boundary; runtime package/path changes but subprocess cardinality remains one.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runtime discovers the two explicit built-in skill directories during session launch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two deduplicated built-in directories per create/resume, plus existing user/plugin skill directories after grouping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The standalone runtime owned and exposed these same two supported built-in skills without host-supplied directory paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session initialization may read these small skill manifests before use, but the prior standalone runtime already exposed the same supported built-in skills and snapshots preserve their prompt surface.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or resume an SDK session with tools, skills, hooks, and plugin directories
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create/resume request per session launch; plugin and skill inputs are deduplicated where applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One create/resume request with existing plugin directories and customization metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing required session startup request; richer metadata does not add request fan-out.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Runtime probes are constant-sized. Session metadata scales with configured plugins, while this diff adds exactly two built-in skill directories after set deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Client startup is globally coalesced through `_clientStarting`/`_ensureClientHealing`; session launches use the existing launcher behavior. No new aggregate process burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm client acquisition returns the existing client and skips all probes/spawn. Filesystem probes benefit from OS cache but are not memoized across actual client restarts. Skill content is owned by the runtime/session lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the startup path and cardinalities; lower for runtime-internal skill parsing duration, which is not needed for the verdict.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact local filesystem and runtime skill-discovery costs are unmeasured, but multiplicity is constant and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: additional local probes and two skill paths are bounded, while process and session boundary cardinality remain unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Executing directory-backed plugin hooks during prompts and tool calls
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The session now explicitly registers hooks from all plugins. When the runtime invokes a hook callback, matching commands execute sequentially before the prompt/tool phase can continue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute configured plugin hook shell commands
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential subprocess per configured command for the invoked hook type, stopping early only where a valid JSON result is accepted; the E2E assertion verifies each directory-backed hook event is invoked exactly once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hooks belonging to file-backed plugins were excluded from the explicit SDK callback map; plugin directory discovery did not register those commands on that callback surface.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pre-tool and prompt hooks block their corresponding operation by design; post/session hooks follow their declared semantics.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the user-configured number and duration of hook commands and with prompt/tool-event frequency, not with unrelated plugin contents.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Commands within one hook type are intentionally serialized; callback invocation is exactly once rather than duplicated between directory discovery and explicit projection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no command-result cache; each declared hook invocation intentionally reruns its commands. Session hook configuration is built once per launch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for subprocess execution and serialization; these are the intended semantics of enabling previously inactive directory-backed hooks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: User hook counts and durations vary widely, but the diff's exact-once callback cardinality is tested.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: the boundary cost is intrinsic to the newly supported hook behavior, ordering is required, and the diff avoids duplicate invocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Product build, cross-platform packaging, and canary override
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Build jobs resolve the SDK runtime version, ensure one target platform package, filter/package native files, and for universal macOS builds cross-copy the opposite architecture package.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `npm view` for SDK canary/runtime metadata and npm lockfile refresh operations
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runtime-version lookup when an SDK override is supplied, plus existing lockfile refresh work per root/remote target when dependency versions change; removed code previously issued additional dependency/range lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: SDK/CLI inference and compatibility checks could issue multiple npm-view subprocess/network calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Build-only network/subprocess work; the diff reduces metadata lookup fan-out rather than increasing it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate required SDK runtime files and package/cross-copy the selected platform package
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five existence checks per ensured target package and one platform-directory cross-copy per architecture/base in universal builds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ensured, filtered, and cross-copied the standalone Copilot platform package instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Build/package critical path only; replaces equivalent standalone runtime package handling with bounded SDK package handling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Costs scale with the fixed set of build targets and two node_modules bases in universal packaging, not workspace/user data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-target packaging remains governed by existing build job parallelism; no new unbounded concurrent npm, copy, or subprocess loop is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal node_modules/build caches remain; canary manifest changes intentionally invalidate the package cache. No runtime user cache is affected.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary counts and build-only reachability.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK and standalone package byte sizes may differ, but the diff provides no evidence of a material build regression and operation counts remain bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: package ownership changes while build operation multiplicity stays bounded, and canary registry calls decrease.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sending Copilot model requests with skill metadata
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session prompt construction serializes instructions and tool schemas, then the runtime sends them with each model request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize built-in skill names/descriptions into the model request prompt/tool schema
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two supported built-in skills per session/request, deduplicated by directory; request count is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The standalone runtime already exposed the same two built-in skills; snapshots show their metadata moved from instructions into the skill tool description rather than adding a second copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Payload bytes remain on the existing model-request network path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Copilot runtime model request represented by the prompt E2E snapshots
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the model request to the provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing model request per turn/model call; no additional call is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same model-request cardinality with the prior runtime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing dominant turn boundary; no request fan-out from this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Payload cost is constant for the two retained built-ins and otherwise scales with existing project/plugin skills and tools.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged runtime request scheduling; no new per-skill network call or subprocess is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session configuration is rebuilt on create/resume; no changed request cache is evident. The runtime owns prompt assembly.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that skill count is two and request cardinality is unchanged; insufficient evidence that unrelated runtime prompt revisions create a host-caused regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact token delta from broader runtime prompt revisions varies by model, but the changed snapshots do not establish duplicate skill metadata or an added request.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: richer metadata is not duplicated and does not change expensive-boundary cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 47 changed files and paginated patches. One low-severity latency regression was reported: model changes now wait on a coalesced but real background catalog network request. Runtime startup probes, session skills, plugin hooks, packaging, prompt serialization, cleanup, cache behavior, and concurrency were traced; no other changed mechanism met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
